incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: "router_p95_latency > 1500ms for 2m" (PD: PGR-3098)
pagerduty: paging oncall rotation: maria
maria: ACK — jumping on it. grabbing metrics and canaries
sam: @maria i'm seeing a small flurry of router restarts in kube events around 01:12 UTC, could be rolling update or node churn
infra-bot: kube event: pod/router-7bd9 restarted on node-a1 (OOMkilled=false) reason=Evicted; reason_detail=NodeNotReady briefly
maria: logs from router instance 10.46.2.71 around spike:
```
2026-03-15T01:11:38Z WARN slow request path=/v1/chat prompt_tokens=1024 latency_ms=1980
2026-03-15T01:11:40Z INFO reclaiming cache shard user=svc-ingest
2026-03-15T01:11:41Z ERROR connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T01:11:42Z INFO cpu=88% pid=2222
```
tess: canaries showed a couple failures at 01:11:37 then recovered at 01:11:50 — looks like ~13s blip
maria: interesting — PD fired at 01:13 for 2m window, but the actual runtime blip was shorter. looks like alert debounce too sensitive
sam: i'm seeing a tight spike on router p95 coincident with a short KV cache thrash (evictions). possibly warmup after eviction + a brief scheduling stall
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert acknowledged by maria at 01:13:05Z
pagerduty: escalation not triggered (no escalation within 5m)
maria: short term mitigations:
- temporarily silence PD escalation for this alert group to avoid noisy wakeups (silence 10m)
- increase alert window to 4m for p95_latency
- pin router pods away from nodes under recent churn (taint tolerance adjustment)
sam: i've applied a 10m silence and bumped alert threshold to 4m in ops-config, will open infra ticket to revisit thresholds
- Ops change: `opsctl alert update router_p95_latency --window=4m --escalation=10m`
infra-bot: changelog entry created: CL-7882 (ops-config)
tess: are customers impacted? Zendesk shows one transient 504 at 01:11:45 from PartnerCorp integration, no widespread errors
maria: marking as POSSIBLE CUSTOMER IMPACT — single partner 504s during the blip. tracking in incident notes.
sam: filed follow-up INF-2032: "investigate KV eviction pattern & autoscaler interaction" https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-2032
maria: quick root-cause hypothesis: eviction -> cache warmup -> short latency spike amplified by pod scheduling jitter. will validate with flamegraphs and pod placement logs
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert auto-resolved at 01:14:38Z (duration 3m6s)
maria: alert cleared. monitoring will keep extra sensitivity off for next 30m. handing off to next oncall in 10m: @sam please take if it reappears, otherwise i'll close INF-2032 after postmortem notes
tess: suggested longer-term fixes: smoother cache eviction policy, increase cache prewarming, and adjust autoscaler cooldowns
sam: agree. added runbook step: "If router p95 spikes coincide with pod evictions, check eviction logs and temporarily pin pods. Escalate to infra if multiple partners show 5xx." I'll put in Confluence.
maria: last check — canaries green, PartnerCorp retried and succeeded, CPU back to baseline. moving to monitoring state.
infra-bot: oncall handoff scheduled: maria -> sam at 01:24Z
maria: thanks team. closing thread here unless PD fires again. :white_check_mark:
